storyLead: How Teknoppy shaped the Instagram and Facebook presence of a business hotel next to Vyttila Metro — built around what a traveller actually wants to know before booking a room in Kochi.
atAGlance: Instagram and Facebook run as one connected presence, with the same hotel name, location, and contact details on both
Content planned around the questions guests ask: where the hotel is, how far it is from the metro, airport, and railway station, and what the stay is like
Location advantage placed first: 200 metres from Vyttila Metro Station and Mobility Hub
Content for both business travellers and leisure guests, so neither audience is ignored
Every post leads to one clear next step: the hotel's own booking and enquiry details
aboutParagraphs: Alankar Avenue is a hotel on Kaniyambuzha Road in Vyttila, Kochi, run under the KSR Alankar Hotels & Resorts Group. It serves business and leisure travellers who want a comfortable stay with good value, and its position is its strongest practical point: the hotel sits about 200 metres from Vyttila Metro Station and the Mobility Hub, roughly 3 km from Ernakulam Junction, and about 22 km from Cochin International Airport.

For a hotel like this, most social media attention comes from people who are already planning a Kochi trip. They look at the Instagram profile to see what the rooms look like, check the location, and decide whether to book directly or keep scrolling. The profile works as a second front door, often visited before the website, so what it shows and how clearly it answers basic questions affects the booking decision.

This case study covers the Instagram and Facebook work delivered by Teknoppy: how the profiles are structured, what the content is built around, and how the two platforms support one another. It does not cover hotel operations, room pricing, or guest services, which belong to Alankar Avenue.
challengeLead: Key challenges addressed during the social media engagement:

challenges.title: A strong location needed to be easy to see
challenges.description: Being 200 metres from a metro station is a real selling point for a traveller moving around Kochi, but it only helps if people notice it quickly, on the profile and in the posts.

challenges.title: Two different guests, one profile
challenges.description: A business traveller on a short work trip and a family on a leisure visit look for different things. The content had to speak to both without confusing either.

challenges.title: Kochi has many hotels competing for the same guest
challenges.description: Travellers compare several properties in a few minutes. A profile that looks generic loses that comparison to one that shows real rooms, real surroundings, and clear information.

challenges.title: Instagram and Facebook were doing separate jobs
challenges.description: Each platform draws a slightly different audience, but both needed to carry the same hotel details so a guest finds consistent information wherever they look.

challenges.title: Interest needed a clear way to become a booking
challenges.description: A guest who likes a post should not have to hunt for how to enquire. The path from profile to phone call or booking had to be obvious.

objectiveLead: Teknoppy was engaged to manage and plan the hotel's Instagram and Facebook presence so that it helps travellers choose, trust, and contact Alankar Avenue. The brief centred on:
objectives: Making the Vyttila Metro and Mobility Hub location the first thing a visitor understands
Creating content for both business and leisure guests
Keeping hotel details identical across Instagram, Facebook, and the website
Showing the property honestly, so what a guest sees online matches what they find on arrival
Giving every post and profile a clear route to enquire or book
approachLead: How Teknoppy built an interconnected social media presence tailored to traveller decision-making:

approachPillars.title: Location treated as the headline
paragraphs: The distance to Vyttila Metro Station, Ernakulam Junction, and Cochin International Airport is practical information a guest uses to plan a day in Kochi. It is stated plainly in the profile and returned to in content, so a traveller does not need to open a map to work out whether the hotel suits their trip.

approachPillars.title: Content themes built around guest questions
paragraphs: Posts are planned around what people actually want to see before booking: the rooms, the property, the surroundings, and how easy it is to get around from the hotel. Each theme answers a question a guest would otherwise have to ask by phone or message.

approachPillars.title: Two audiences, handled separately
paragraphs: Business travellers care about access, convenience, and a reliable place to stay between meetings. Leisure guests care about comfort and what is nearby in Kochi. Content is balanced so each group sees something made for them, rather than one message stretched across both.

approachPillars.title: Instagram and Facebook working together
paragraphs: Both platforms carry the same hotel name, address, and contact details. Instagram leads on visuals, while Facebook suits longer descriptions and information that guests and families often check. Keeping them aligned means a guest gets the same answer on either one.

approachPillars.title: The profile as a booking page
paragraphs: The Instagram profile is set up so a visitor can find the hotel's website and contact details without searching. A guest who decides in the moment can call or message straight away.

approachPillars.title: Consistent naming across every channel
paragraphs: The hotel appears under the same name, with the same address and phone details, across Instagram, Facebook, and its website. Consistency helps people recognise the hotel as one business and helps search and map tools connect the profiles to the same place.

deliverables.description: Clear, consistent profiles with the hotel's name, location, and contact details in place on both platforms.

deliverables.title: A location-first content theme
deliverables.description: Posts and profile information built around the Vyttila Metro and Mobility Hub advantage.

deliverables.title: Content for business and leisure guests
deliverables.description: A content plan balanced across both audiences the hotel serves.

deliverables.title: Guest-question content
deliverables.description: Posts organised around the rooms, property, and surroundings that guests want to see before booking.

deliverables.title: Aligned details across channels
deliverables.description: The same name, address, and contact information on Instagram, Facebook, and the website.

deliverables.title: A clear enquiry route
deliverables.description: An obvious path from profile or post to the hotel's contact and booking details.

whyMattersParagraphs: People rarely book a hotel from a single post. They look at the profile, scroll through recent content, check the location, and compare it with a few other properties, often in the same sitting. A profile that answers their questions quickly, and looks like a real place with real contact details, earns the next step. A profile that is vague or inconsistent sends the guest elsewhere.

The same clarity helps in search. Search engines and AI answer tools now draw on social profiles and business details when they respond to questions such as which hotel is near Vyttila Metro. When the hotel's name, location, and distances are stated the same way everywhere, those tools can describe Alankar Avenue accurately.

Social media does not replace the hotel's website or its search presence, and it works best alongside them. Posting with a plan, rather than whenever there is something to share, is what makes the profile read as a business guests can trust.

faqs.question: Where is Alankar Avenue located in Kochi?
faqs.answer: Alankar Avenue is on Kaniyambuzha Road, Vyttila, Kochi, about 200 metres from Vyttila Metro Station and the Mobility Hub.

faqs.question: How far is Alankar Avenue from Ernakulam Junction and Cochin airport?
faqs.answer: The hotel is roughly 3 km from Ernakulam Junction railway station and about 22 km from Cochin International Airport.

faqs.question: Is Alankar Avenue suitable for business travellers or only for holidays?
faqs.answer: It serves both. The hotel caters to business and leisure travellers, and its social media content is planned for both groups.

faqs.question: Which social media pages does Alankar Avenue run?
faqs.answer: The hotel is on Instagram as @alankar_avenue and on Facebook, with the same name and contact details on both.

faqs.question: Can I contact the hotel directly from its Instagram or Facebook page?
faqs.answer: Yes. The profiles carry the hotel's contact details and a link to its website, so you can call or enquire without searching for them.

faqs.question: Why should a hotel use both Instagram and Facebook?
faqs.answer: The two platforms reach slightly different audiences. Instagram works well for visuals of the rooms and property, and Facebook suits fuller descriptions and details that families and older guests often check.

faqs.question: Does Teknoppy handle social media for other hotels and resorts in Kerala?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy plans and manages Instagram and Facebook for hospitality businesses, with content built around the questions their guests ask before booking.
